AlternateTargets: having no affairs to attend to
Senses.Explanation: Literally (無) (no) + (事) (matter / affair / business): having no matter on hand, nothing that needs doing. Linji Yixuan gives it its sharpest form: (無事是貴人) — the person with nothing to do is the noble person — immediately glossed (但莫造作)，(秖是平常) ('just don't fabricate; only be ordinary'). Linji applies (無事人) even to Buddhas and patriarchs: (佛與祖師是無事人) (Buddhas and patriarchs are people with nothing to do), and glosses it (秖是平常著衣)、(喫飯)、(無事過時) (just ordinarily wearing clothes, eating, passing the time with nothing to do). Huangbo Xiyun, Linji's teacher, states it from the other side: when feelings are exhausted with nothing left to rely on or grasp, that is the (無事人) (情盡都無依執。是無事人); (道人是無事人)，(實無許多般心) (the man of the Way is one with nothing to do, without all those many kinds of mind). Render literally as 'nothing to do': the Chinese says that there is no affair to be done. The (祖堂集) Deshan chapter turns it on the mind: (汝但無事於心)，(無心於事)，(乃虛而妙矣)。(若毫釐繫念)，(皆為自欺) (just be without matter in the mind and without mind in matters, and it is empty and wondrous; a hair's-breadth of tied-on thought is all self-deceit; B25n0144), a line Zhongfeng cites under Deshan's name — (德山謂)。(汝但於心無事無事於心)。(自然虛而靈寂而妙) ('Deshan said: just have no matter in the mind and no mind in matters, and of itself it is empty and numinous, still and wondrous', B25n0145); the chiasmus (無事於心)，(無心於事) ('no matter in the mind, no mind in matters') recurs across 13 texts. The records also deploy the word inside postures they attack: (無事甲) (the nothing-to-do shell, 163 hits in 92 allowlist texts — 坐在無事甲裏 'sitting inside the nothing-to-do shell', 打在無事甲裏 'knocked into the nothing-to-do shell', 置之無事甲中 'put away in the nothing-to-do shell'; Zhongfeng B25n0145, seven hits in Dahui's record T47n1998A), (無事會) (the nothing-to-do understanding, 46/31) — (切不得作無事會去) ('above all do not take it as the nothing-to-do understanding', J26nB186), (若作平常無事會)，(辜負山僧不少) ('if you take it as an ordinary nothing-to-do understanding, you fail this mountain monk badly', J33nB280), (學者不可作無事會)，(若作無事會)，(則著無事魔) ('a student must not take it as the nothing-to-do understanding; take it so, and the nothing-to-do demon takes hold', J25nB163) — and (無事界) (the nothing-to-do realm, 21/15): (未免墮在無事界裏) ('cannot help falling into the nothing-to-do realm', T47n1997). A (黔南會燈錄) verse separates saying from having: (口說無事易)，(心中無事難) (to say nothing-to-do is easy; nothing-to-do in the mind is hard; X85n1591).
Senses.Note: Held identically across teacher and disciple in the Hongzhou line — Huangbo (傳心法要) and Linji (臨濟語錄) — two independent witnesses of the same sense. Linji supplies the stock formula (無事是貴人) and (無事人); kept as one corpus-wide sense because the meaning does not differ between masters. Zen-scoped grep (tag-stripped, 2026-07-11): (無事) 3453 hits in 373 allowlist texts; (無事人) 253/109; the exact formula (無事是貴人) 6 hits in 6 texts (T47n1985, C077n1710, X78n1553, X79n1557, J23nB134, J34nB301) — it circulates beyond Linji's own record. The criticized-posture collocations quoted in the explanation count (無事甲) 163/92, (無事會) 46/31, (無事界) 21/15.

Occurrences.Kwic: 無事是貴人，但莫造作，秖是平常
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (師示眾) (Linji addressing the assembly), (鎮州臨濟慧照禪師語錄). The stock formula.

Occurrences.Kwic: 佛與祖師是無事人
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Linji: even Buddhas and patriarchs are 'people with nothing to do' (佛與祖師是無事人).

Occurrences.Kwic: 秖是平常著衣、喫飯、無事過時
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Linji's gloss: nothing to do is just wearing clothes, eating, passing the time.

Occurrences.Kwic: 道人是無事人。實無許多般心
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (上堂) ('ascending the hall'; Huangbo), (黃檗山斷際禪師傳心法要). The man of the Way is one with nothing to do — no manifold mind.

Occurrences.Kwic: 情盡都無依執。是無事人
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Huangbo's definition from the exhaustion side: feelings spent, nothing to rely on or grasp — that is the person with nothing to do.

Senses.Explanation: Literally, a person with no affairs or nothing going on. Several Chan records define the phrase directly. Guishan says that when bad notions, feelings, views, imaginings, and habits are absent, one is like autumn water standing clear, clean, inactive, tranquil, and unobstructed: such a person is called a person of the Way and also a person with nothing going on. Baizhang says that not being confused or disordered, angry or delighted at each object, and cleaning up at the gates of one's six faculties is being a person with nothing going on. Another recorded statement says that when inner and outer feelings are dissolved and exhausted, with no dependence or grasping, this is a person with nothing going on. Linji says that seeing as he has described leaves one a person with nothing going on for life. The record also supplies corrections: one line says even an inactive person with nothing going on remains a difficult golden lock; a teacher quotes his predecessor saying that buddha is a person with nothing going on, then adds that such a person cannot now be found; and Muzhou invites forward a person with nothing going on, only to send the approaching monk outside for twenty blows.
Senses.Note: The corpus has 253 matches in 109 files. Naming constructions have two matches in two files for 'called a person with nothing going on,' four in four for 'named,' and twenty-four in twenty-three for 'called.' 'Buddha is a person with nothing going on' occurs five times in five files; 'an inactive person with nothing going on' occurs seventy-six times in forty-three, and the corrective 'a person with nothing going on remains a difficult golden lock' occurs twice in two. The neighboring formula 'having nothing going on is the honored person' occurs six times in six files. The entry retains both the definitions and the record's explicit checks on adopting the label too quickly.

Occurrences.Kwic: 若無如許多惡覺情見想習之事，譬如秋水澄渟，清淨無為，澹泞無礙。喚他作道人，亦名無事人。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Guishan says, 'If there are none of those many bad notions, feelings, views, imaginings, and habits, one is like autumn water standing clear: clean, inactive, tranquil, and unobstructed. Call him a person of the Way; he is also named a person with nothing going on.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 秖如今於一一境，不惑不亂，不瞋不喜，於自己六根門頭刮削，併當得淨潔，是無事人
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Baizhang says, 'Right now, at each and every object, not confused, not disordered, not angry, not delighted; scrape and clean at the gates of your own six faculties until they are clean—this is a person with nothing going on.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 但消融表裏情盡都無依執是無事人
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A record states, 'Only dissolve inner and outer; when feelings are exhausted and there is no dependence or grasping at all, this is a person with nothing going on.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 若能如是見得，秖是一生無事人。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Linji says, 'If you can see in this way, you are simply a person with nothing going on for your whole life.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 所以清涼先師道。佛是無事人。且如今覓箇無事人也不可得。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A teacher says, 'Therefore my late teacher Qingliang said, Buddha is a person with nothing going on. Yet now even seeking a person with nothing going on, one cannot be found.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 無為無事人。猶是金鎖難。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A line says, 'An inactive person with nothing going on is still a difficult golden lock.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 老僧在此住持。不曾見箇無事人到來。汝等何不近前。時有一僧方近前。師云。維那不在。汝自領出去三門外與二十棒。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Muzhou says, 'In all my time presiding here, I have never seen a person with nothing going on arrive. Why do you not come forward?' When a monk starts forward, Muzhou says, 'The rector is not here. Take yourself outside the triple gate and receive twenty blows.'

Senses.Explanation: Literally, without (無) rank or ordered place (位). Chan turns rank-language into a recurrent predicate and name. Linji's best-known deployment is the 'true person without rank,' said to be on the lump of red flesh and to go in and out through people's face-gates. The bare term functions as an answer: asked 'how is it?' Guanxi says 'without rank'; when challenged whether that is the same as empty space, he replies 'you butcher.' Elsewhere a monk asks why, if he is a teacher, he has no rank/order; the answer says ancient and present cannot arrange it and the three times cannot place it. A rank-system exchange asks, 'when merit is turned and there is no rank, how is it?' and receives 'the royal house's affairs are manifest.' Another address contrasts name and rank with no rank and no name. The Zen deviation is this removal of ordered rank from a public figure, answer, spatial ordering, and formal rank-system question. The standalone entry records that family while leaving Linji's full figure in its own article.
Senses.Note: Exact unsplit count: 1,473 hits in 267 allowlisted texts; true person without rank (無位真人) accounts for 1,259 hits in 250 texts. Without rank/order (無位次) has 91 in 63; originally without rank/order (本無位次) 28 in 25. This Chan rank-language is separated from ordinary lack of institutional position below. Family checked against true person without rank (無位真人), rank/order (位次), with rank (有位), no dependence (無依), red flesh-lump (赤肉團), and rank/position (位).

Occurrences.Kwic: 赤肉團上有一無位真人，常從汝等諸人面門出入，
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Linji's core nested compound: the true person without rank on the red flesh-lump.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問灌溪。作麼生。溪曰。無位。師曰。莫同虗空麼。溪曰。這屠兒。師曰。有生可殺即不倦。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Bare answer in a public exchange, immediately challenged against empty space.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問。既是師。為甚却無位次。師曰。古今排不出。三際豈能安。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Direct question about a teacher without rank/order; answer denies arrangement by ancient/present or the three times.

Occurrences.Kwic: 有名有位，東西相對；無位無名，大地平沉。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Text-drawn named/ranked versus nameless/rankless contrast.

Occurrences.Kwic: 不得商量，不涉文墨。本絕塵境，本無位次。權名箇出家兒，畢竟無踪迹。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Prose predicate: originally without rank/order, followed by only provisionally naming a person who has left home.

Occurrences.Kwic: 曰。轉功無位時如何。師曰。王家事宛然。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Formal rank-system public question: turning merit when without rank.

Senses.Explanation: In ordinary institutional description, (無位) says that a person has virtue but holds no recognized position. The absence concerns public standing and evidentiary authority, not the Chan rank-system or Linji's rankless true person.
Senses.Note: One allowlisted source presently anchors this distinct institutional referent, so the sense remains provisional.

Occurrences.Kwic: 即有知而闢之者，有德無位。一人之言，無徵不信。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A critic is described as having virtue but no position; the following clause says one person's word lacks corroboration.

AlternateTargets: a true person of no rank
Senses.Explanation: Literally 'a true person of no rank' — (位) is rank/office/status (the graded positions of the bureaucracy, or of ranked stages). Linji coins it in his most famous (上堂): 「(赤肉團上有一無位真人)，(常從汝等諸人面門出入)」 — 'on your lump of red flesh there is one true person of no rank, forever going in and out through your face and sense-gates'; those who have not yet witnessed it, 'look! look!' (未證據者看看). When a monk asks 「(如何是無位真人)」 and hesitates, Linji shoves him off (師托開) and says 「(無位真人是什麼乾屎橛)」 — 'the true person of no rank — what a dried shit-stick!' The phrase is transmitted verbatim in the (古尊宿語錄) Linji section and taken up corpus-wide as a stock figure (e.g. 西臺辯 「舉臨濟無位真人語」; a later gloss: 「無位真人突出難辨。頂門上時時顯現，眼睛裏處處…」 — it shows itself on the crown of the head and in the pupils of the eyes). The opening line recurs verbatim across the record — (赤肉團上有一無位真人), 87 hits in 71 allowlist texts — and (如何是無位真人) becomes a standing test-question in its own right (141 hits in 96 texts): the (靈機禪師語錄) answers it "met face to face" (覿面相逢), and when the questioner counters "what is the true person WITH rank?" (如何是有位真人) the master strikes (師打，云：「棒打不回頭。」) and, as the monk hesitates, adds "this dead true person — what is it good for?" (者死真人堪作甚麼). Compilations set it beside other masters' signature answers: (雲門喚作乾矢橛)，(洞山喚作麻三斤)，(趙州喚作柏樹子)，(臨濟喚作無位真人) (J34nB298). The Qing (御選語錄) carries a discursive gloss of the name — asked (如何是無位真人) the speaker answers "greed" (貪), then: "'true person of no rank': not originally rank-less — it is forcibly named 'no rank'. Say he has rank, and that is precisely no rank; say he has no rank, and that is precisely rank. To know the true person of no rank you must get it from within rank" (言無位真人者，本非無位，強名之曰無位耳。若言有位，却是無位。說他無位，却是有位。要識無位真人，須從有位中會). Always credited to Linji.
Senses.Note: Distinctively Linji's coinage; uniqueness is NOT disputed (unlike the buffalo/異類中行 case) — every later occurrence explicitly frames it as (臨濟)'s saying. Kept as a null corpus-wide sense because the phrase circulates as a stock figure across the corpus (241 allowlist texts), but its origin and reading are Linji's throughout. Reception evidence (allowlist grep): the raising-formula (舉臨濟)…(無位真人) appears in 11 texts (14 hits), and (喚作無位真人) credits it to (臨濟) by name in 6 texts — including (尀耐臨濟賊漢)，(喚作無位真人) ('insufferable thief Linji — calling it the true person of no rank', X68n1318 續刊古尊宿語要; echoed X70n1375). The record also sets it against Huairang's (說似一物即不中): (古人道)：『(喚作一物即不中)。』(如何又喚作無位真人)？」(師云)：「(你即今是一物)？(是無位真人)？ (J10nA158 密雲禪師語錄). The counter-term (有位真人) is attested only 6 times in 2 texts (J39nB448; X68n1319's gloss, which builds the name from it).

Occurrences.Kwic: 赤肉團上有一無位真人
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (臨濟錄) (Record of Linji). Linji's (上堂) (上堂云): the locus classicus. Continues on the next line 「(常從汝等諸人面門出入)，(未證據者看看)」 (kept out of the KWIC to avoid crossing the line break).

Occurrences.Kwic: 無位真人是什麼乾屎橛
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (臨濟錄). Same exchange: after the questioning monk hesitates (其僧擬議), Linji pushes him away (師托開) and says (無位真人是什麼乾屎橛) (dried shit-stick). Linji's own words.

Occurrences.Kwic: 上堂云赤肉團上有一無位真人常
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (古尊宿語錄), in the Linji section (nearest 卷 head: 「臨濟慧照禪師諱義玄…」). Independent transmission of the same (上堂) — second witness that this is Linji's.

Occurrences.Kwic: 西臺辯禪師上堂，舉臨濟無位真人語
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Later master (西臺辯) (Xitai Bian) 'raises Linji's true-person-of-no-rank saying' (舉臨濟…語) in his own (上堂). MasterName null because the act is the quoting master's and the line explicitly credits (臨濟) — reception evidence that the term is Linji's.

Occurrences.Kwic: 無位真人突出難辨。頂門上時時顯現，眼睛裏處處
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A later gloss echoing Linji's 'goes in and out through the sense-gates' — the true person shows itself on the crown of the head and in the pupils of the eyes.

Senses.Explanation: Literally, 'no dwelling' or 'not abiding.' The raw headword occurs 1,252 times in 239 allowed texts; that total includes both the phrase and the personal name Wuzhu. Huineng gives the fullest direct description of the phrase: 'Not dwelling is people's original nature' (無住者，人之本性). He continues through good and bad, beautiful and ugly, hostile and friendly, and verbal conflict, saying not to think of former objects from thought to thought. He then names the contrast: if former, present, and later thoughts continue without break, this is called binding; 'from thought to thought, not dwelling on all things is no binding—this is taking not-dwelling as the root' (於諸法上念念不住，即無縛也。此是以無住為本). Fayan's recorded case begins from the line 'from the root of not-dwelling establish all things'; asked what that root is, Fayan answers, 'form arises before substance; name arises before naming' (形興未質，名起未名). Wansong's case commentary preserves another explicit exchange: asked what the root of not-dwelling rests on, the answer is 'not-dwelling has no root' (無住則無本). In the Shenhui and Huineng encounter, Shenhui says, 'Take not-dwelling as the root; seeing is the master' (以無住為本。見即是主). Later records pair 'not-dwelling as root' with 'no-thought as source' and call the root of not-dwelling the root of all things. The recurring grammar is verbal and relational: thoughts do not dwell, a root does not itself rest on another root, and things are said to be established from it.
Senses.Note: The direct Huineng definition, the Fayan public case, Shenhui's reply, and later comments are retained as distinct witnesses. 'Without a place to dwell' (無所住) occurs 370 times in 145 texts; 'not-dwelling as the root' (無住為本) occurs 44 times in 27; 'root of not-dwelling' (無住本) occurs 135 times in 64; and 'not-dwelling mind' (無住心) occurs 38 times in 30. Biographical occurrences where these two graphs form the name Wuzhu were excluded from semantic evidence.

Occurrences.Kwic: 無住者，人之本性。於世間善惡好醜，乃至冤之與親，言語觸刺欺爭之時，並將為空，不思酬害，念念之中不思前境。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Platform Record, stability-and-discernment section. Huineng directly calls not-dwelling people's original nature and describes its deployment amid opposed conditions and verbal conflict.

Occurrences.Kwic: 若前念今念後念，念念相續不斷，名為繫縛。於諸法上念念不住，即無縛也。此是以無住為本。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Huineng immediately contrasts uninterrupted continuation, which he calls binding, with thought after thought not dwelling on all things.

Occurrences.Kwic: 舉僧問法眼。承教有言。從無住本立一切法。如何是無住本。眼云。形興未質名起未名。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Hongzhi's record raises Fayan's public case and then verses it. Because it is a raised two-speaker case, MasterName remains null.

Occurrences.Kwic: 又問無住孰為本。答無住則無本。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Wansong's commentary on Fayan's case quotes the earlier chain of questions and the answer that not-dwelling has no root. It remains a raised dialogue.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師曰。以無住為本。見即是主。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Five Lamps Compendium, Heze Shenhui section. Shenhui gives this answer to Huineng; the two-speaker encounter remains unkeyed.

Occurrences.Kwic: 是故文殊以無住為本，曹溪以無念為宗。無念之宗為萬法之宗，無住之本為萬法之本。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Five Lamps Complete Collection. An assembly address pairs Manjusri's not-dwelling root with Caoxi's no-thought source and relates each to all things. No roster link was asserted.

Senses.PreferredTarget: the person of the Way with no reliance
AlternateTargets: the no-reliance person of the Way
the person on the Way who relies on nothing
Senses.Explanation: Literally, a person of the Way (道人) with no reliance (無依). Linji repeatedly identifies this figure with the person presently listening to the teaching: 'the person of the Way with no reliance who is listening to the teaching right now' (現今目前聽法無依道人), plainly distinct and never lacking. He calls this person 'the mother of the buddhas' (是諸佛之母), says buddhas are born from no reliance, and says buddha-settings cannot name themselves—the person with no reliance rides the setting and comes out. He further says that although this person is the leaky substance of the five aggregates, it is earth-walking spiritual power, and that moving and not moving are two settings used by this person. The Zen bend is Linji's relocation of an apparently wandering ascetic title into the live teaching assembly: it names the hearer before him and the invariant person that uses changing named settings. Later records overwhelmingly quote, explain, challenge, and even warn against holding to this Linji formula; this distinct formulation therefore remains master-keyed.
Senses.Note: The corpus has 73 exact occurrences in 32 allowlisted files. Linji's own record supplies the distinct sense; independent lamp and collected-record witnesses preserve the same statements, while later masters quote and criticize the formula. This is not a generic biographical title: some late occurrences do use 'Person of the Way with No Reliance' as a literary sobriquet, but those are secondary name uses and do not displace Linji's technical deployment.

Occurrences.Kwic: 唯有聽法無依道人，是諸佛之母，所以佛從無依生。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Linji's own record: the person listening to the teaching with no reliance is called the mother of the buddhas, and buddhas are said to be born from no reliance.

Occurrences.Kwic: 還是這箇無依道人乘境出來。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Linji says a buddha-setting cannot call itself a buddha-setting; this person rides the setting and comes out.

Occurrences.Kwic: 現今目前聽法無依道人歷歷地分明，未曾欠少。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Linji locates the figure directly in the hall: the person now before his eyes listening to the teaching is plainly distinct and has never lacked anything.

Occurrences.Kwic: 此無依道人，雖是五蘊漏質，便是地行神通。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Linji predicates both the leaky substance of the five aggregates and earth-walking spiritual power of the same person.

Occurrences.Kwic: 佛境不能自稱我是佛境，還是者箇無依道人乘境出來。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Heavenly Sage Expanded Lamp independently transmits Linji's setting-and-rider formulation.

AlternateTargets: an iron hammer without an eye
Senses.Explanation: Literally, “an iron hammer without a hole.” The phrase occurs 256 times in 108 allowlisted texts. The missing hole is the missing eye by which a hammer head takes its handle; the records repeatedly deploy the resulting solid object as an image of something with no entry point. It appears in similes—“water cannot wet it and wind cannot enter it, like a holeless iron hammer” (水灑不著，風吹不入，如箇無孔鐵鎚相似)—and as a direct answer to “What thing can heaven not cover and earth not support?” Later comments apply the same object-image to answers and exchanges, including “a holeless iron hammer driving in a wedge again” (無孔鐵鎚重下楔). These are uses of the object-image, distinct from passages that directly call people holeless iron hammers.
Senses.Note: Primary Zen-loaded sense first. The entry states the construction visible in the graphs and the corpus's own water/wind predicates; it does not assign the image a mystical meaning. The ordinary tool is not independently attested as an actual implement in the harvested passages.

Occurrences.Kwic: 直得水灑不著，風吹不入，如箇無孔鐵鎚相似。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The text itself supplies the impermeability comparison.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問：天不能葢，地不能載，是甚麼物？師曰：無孔鐵鎚。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A public interview records the phrase as a direct answer naming a thing.

Occurrences.Kwic: 對一說太孤絕無孔鐵鎚重下楔閻浮樹下笑呵呵昨夜驪龍拗角折
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Blue Cliff Record preserves Xuedou's verse using the hammer-and-wedge wording.

Occurrences.Kwic: 盡十方世界是箇無孔鐵鎚，迦葉不知。無汝擬議處，無汝承當處
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A sermon extends the object-image to the whole world and immediately says there is no place for deliberation or undertaking.

Senses.Explanation: The same compound also directly labels people rather than merely comparing another object or statement with a hammer. Masters address an assembly as “this squad of holeless iron hammers” (這一隊無孔鐵鎚), dismiss a non-answering visitor with “Holeless iron hammer—go to the hall!”, and say that two old masters are “a pair of holeless iron hammers.” Here the grammatical referent is a person or pair of people, so this person-label is split from the object-image rather than blurred into one gloss.
Senses.Note: This split follows the different-thing test: an object/image in sense 1, people directly named by the phrase in sense 2. It is not a split between interpretations of the same passage.

Occurrences.Kwic: 遂拈拄杖，云：這一隊無孔鐵鎚，速退，速退。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The plural classifier and dismissal directly label members of the assembly.

Occurrences.Kwic: 主云：經論無文所載。師云：無孔鐵鎚。參堂去！
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The master applies the epithet directly to a visitor and sends him to the hall.

Occurrences.Kwic: 正對得趙州答此僧話。渾似兩箇無孔鐵鎚。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Yuanwu calls the two masters in the compared exchanges two holeless iron hammers.

Senses.PreferredTarget: the word ‘no’ — Zhaozhou’s answer raised for investigation
Senses.Explanation: Literally 'the word ‘no’ (無).' Not the bare negation and not 'wordless' — it names Zhaozhou's single spoken ‘no’ (無) (from the case 狗子還有佛性也無？州云無, 'does a dog have Buddha-nature? — No') taken up as the word to be investigated. The corpus almost always says (箇無字) ('this one word ‘no’ (無)') or (無字話) ('the case of ‘no’ (無)'), and the Song-era instruction is (看箇無字) / (參箇無字) ('look at / investigate the word ‘no’ (無) [no]'). Wumen enshrines it as case 1 of the (無門關) (the Gateless Barrier): (如何是祖師關)？(只者一箇無字)，(乃宗門一關也) ('what is the ancestral barrier? — just this one word ‘no’ (無), the single barrier of our school'), and prescribes (通身起箇疑團)，(參箇無字)，(晝夜提撕)，(莫作虛無會)，(莫作有無會) ('with your whole body raise one mass of doubt, investigate the word ‘no’ (無), keep bringing it up day and night — do NOT construe it as nihilistic void, nor as the "no" of has-versus-hasn't'). Dahui repeatedly tells readers to ‘look at a saying’ (看話) and later records use the label ‘Chan of looking at sayings’ (看話禪): (州云無)。(只這一字)，(便是斷生死路頭底刀子也) ('Zhaozhou said No — just this one word is the knife that cuts off the road of life and death'); when thoughts stir, (但舉箇無字) ('just raise the word ‘no’ (無)'). Gaofeng records watching it three years straight (前所看無字，將及三載). The texts themselves call it a (關) (barrier) of the school and warn against construing it as nihilistic void (莫作虛無會) or as the has/has-not 'no' (莫作有無會). The word even names the book: having called (無) the one barrier of the school, the text adds (遂目之曰禪宗無門關) ('hence it was titled the Chan school's Gateless Barrier'). Wumen's commentary stays at the level of the single word: (如吞了箇熱鐵丸)。(相似吐又吐不出) ('like having swallowed a red-hot iron ball that you cannot spit back out'), (盡平生氣力)。(舉箇無字) ('with the whole strength of your life, raise the word ‘no’ (無)'); his verse runs (狗子佛性)。(全提正令)。(纔涉有無)。(喪身失命) ('the dog's Buddha-nature: the standing order fully presented — the moment you engage has-or-hasn't, you lose body and life'). In later usage the case is tagged by the word itself: (趙州無字) ('Zhaozhou's word 無 [no]'), (無字話) ('the saying of ‘no’ (無)'), (無字公案) ('the case of ‘no’ (無)').
Senses.Note: Distinct entry from the bare particle (無) (negation) and from literal (無字) = 'no words / wordless' (e.g. 無字碑, a blank stele). §5b: the relation (無字) → (無) is REAL, not a coincidental prefix — (無字) literally means 'the word ‘no’ (無),' i.e. Zhaozhou's actual utterance. Multi-source: Wumen Huikai (無門關, the Gateless Barrier), Dahui Zonggao (大慧語錄, Dahui's recorded sayings), Gaofeng Yuanmiao (禪要, Essentials of Chan), and many later masters use it identically. Anti-fakeout: the primary texts themselves forbid reading it as 'nothingness/void' (莫作虛無會). Cross-ref the (佛性) entry (t_ad0a8e5aac3d, sense 2) and (狗子無佛性) — the case this word comes from. Collocation counts (462-text allowlist grep; raw string counts, sense-blind): (無字) 782 hits in 174 texts; (箇無字) 139 in 44; (無字話) 94 in 31; (趙州無字) 71 in 34; (無字公案) 17 in 12; (看箇無字) 12 in 11; (舉箇無字) 4 in 3; (參箇無字) 4 in 3; the source case (狗子無佛性) 358 in 105. (遂目之曰禪宗無門關) and the (熱鐵丸) simile: T48n2005 0292c27–0293a13.

Occurrences.Kwic: 如何是祖師關。只者一箇無字。乃宗門一關也。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (無門關) case 1 commentary (無門曰): the word ‘no’ (無) IS the barrier of the school.

Occurrences.Kwic: 通身起箇疑團。參箇無字。晝夜提撕。莫作虛無會。莫作有無會。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The instruction + the guard: not nihilistic void (虛無), not the has/has-not 'no' (有無).

Occurrences.Kwic: 州云無。只這一字。便是斷生死路頭底刀子也。妄念起時。但舉箇無字。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (大慧語錄); the word ‘no’ (無) as the knife cutting life and death, and Dahui’s literal instruction.

Occurrences.Kwic: 不用作佛法想。但只看狗子無佛性話。但只舉箇無字。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Ties (無字) explicitly to the (狗子無佛性) case; 'just raise the word ‘no’ (無).'

Occurrences.Kwic: 前所看無字，將及三載，除二時粥飯不曾上蒲團，困時亦不倚靠。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (禪要); Gaofeng recounts looking at the word ‘no’ (無) for nearly three years — third independent master.

Senses.Explanation: (無) = no / without; (心) = mind. (無心) is literally "no mind." Huangbo defines it flatly: "no-mind means: no mind of any kind at all" (無心者無一切心也), glossing it "simply have no arising-mind, no stirring-thought, no mind of being/non-being, long/short, self/other, subject/object" (但無生心動念有無長短彼我能所等心); in (傳心法要) this definition is given as the stated reason (何故, "why?") for the aphorism it directly follows: "making offerings to the buddhas of the ten directions does not equal making an offering to one no-mind man of the Way" (供養十方諸佛。不如供養一個無心道人). He states "if you can just be no-mind, that is the ultimate" (但能無心便是究竟), and the stock phrase "no-mind is the Way" (無心是道) is attested across 33 Zen texts of the allowlist. The record adds "the mind is of itself no-mind; nor is there any 'one who is no-mind'" (心自無心，亦無無心者) and "using mind to be no-mind already makes it something existent" (將心無心，心却成有). Dahui Zonggao's instruction to layman Qingjing (示清淨居士, 大慧普覺禪師法語卷十九) carries the corpus's fullest self-definition, negative then positive: "what is called no-mind is not being insensately blank like earth, wood, tile, or stone; it means that touching situations and meeting conditions, the mind stays settled, unmoving, and does not grasp at anything" (所謂無心者。非如土木瓦石頑然無知。謂觸境遇緣。心定不動。不取著諸法), concluding "only on reaching such a state is it first called true no-mind — and not a no-mind said at the mouth" (到得如此境界。方始謂之真無心。且非口頭說底無心): "if one has not attained true no-mind and goes only by the saying, how does it differ from the false Chan of silent illumination?" (若未得真無心。只據說底。與默照邪禪。何以異哉). Asked at his death who receives the eye of the teaching (正法眼藏，傳付何人), the Sixth Patriarch answers "one who has the Way obtains it; one with no mind penetrates it" (有道者得，無心者通) — carried in the (壇經) (the Platform Scripture), the (景德傳燈錄) (the Jingde-era Record of the Transmission of the Lamp), and five later lamp records of the allowlist (the 祖堂集, the Collection from the Patriarchs' Hall, reads 有道者得，無心者得, 'one who has the Way obtains it; one with no mind obtains it'). Sikongshan Benjing, a disciple of the Sixth Patriarch, defends the phrase in open court debate before the emperor: he answers Chan-master Yuan's (遠禪師) charge of self-contradiction — that (無心是道) and (身心本來是道) conflict — with (無心是道)，(心泯道無)，(心道一如); and when a later challenger, Zhiming (志明禪師), objects that tiles and pebbles are equally mindless (瓦礫無心亦應是道), Benjing answers (窮本不有)…(焉得不同草木瓦礫), whereupon Zhiming falls silent.
Senses.Note: Distinguish from the plain-language (無心) = 'unintentionally / with no intent' (as in 有心/無心), which is not the recorded sense described here — the raw string (~4,300 hits in 370 allowlist texts) is sense-blind across the two. Huangbo's (傳心法要) / (宛陵錄) is the locus classicus; (本淨) (Huineng's lineage) is an independent early witness. Attested collocations (allowlist grep): (無心道人) 122 hits in 57 texts; the offering-aphorism (不如供養一箇)／(一個無心道人) in 17 texts, which the record redeploys as a test-question — (洛浦因僧問供養百千諸佛不如供養一箇無心道人未審百千諸佛有何過無心道人有何德師曰一片白雲橫谷口幾多歸鳥盡迷巢) (Luopu, when a monk asked 'offering to a hundred thousand buddhas does not equal an offering to one no-mind man of the Way — what fault, then, in the hundred thousand buddhas, what virtue in the no-mind man of the Way?', said 'a stretch of white cloud lies across the valley mouth; how many homing birds all lose their nest'; C078n1720; the same exchange raised in J29nB248, J25nB171) — and (如何是無心道人) ('what is a no-mind man of the Way?', 9 texts), answered e.g. (早晨喫薄粥)，(於今猶覺饑) ('this morning I ate thin gruel; even now I still feel hungry'; J29nB229). The record also circulates a verse that negates the slogan's own wording: (莫謂無心云是道)，(無心猶隔一重關) ('do not say that no-mind is the Way — no-mind is still one barrier removed'; 51 hits in 41 texts, also worded 莫謂無心便是道), extended in B27n0152 (說甚一重直是千重萬重) ('what one barrier — a full thousand, ten thousand barriers') and itself asked back as a test-question (未審是那一重關)？ ('which one barrier is it, then?'; J25nB173).

Occurrences.Kwic: 無心者無一切心也。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (黃檗山斷際禪師傳心法要) (Huangbo's Chuanxin Fayao); Huangbo's flat definition — no-mind = no mind of any kind at all.

Occurrences.Kwic: 但能無心。便是究竟。學道人若不直下無心。累劫修行終不成道。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Essential Teaching on Mind Transmission (傳心法要) says that directly being without mind is final, and that without it, even refining for successive ages accomplishes nothing.

Occurrences.Kwic: 此心即法。法外無心。心自無心。亦無無心者。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (傳心法要); mind is of itself no-mind, and there is no 'one who is no-mind' either.

Occurrences.Kwic: 即心是佛。無心是道。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (黃檗斷際禪師宛陵錄) (Huangbo's Wanling lu); the stock phrase (無心是道) paired with (即心是佛), in answer to (如何是佛).

Occurrences.Kwic: 若欲求佛即心是佛。若欲會道無心是道。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (景德傳燈錄), spoken by (司空山本淨) (a disciple of the Sixth Patriarch Huineng) to the emperor's envoy in 744 CE; an independent, Huineng-lineage witness to (無心是道), defended in the ensuing debate.

Occurrences.Kwic: 所謂無心者。非如土木瓦石頑然無知。謂觸境遇緣。心定不動。不取著諸法。一切處蕩然無障無礙。無所染污。亦不住在無染污處。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Dahui's direct definition says that no-mind is not the insensate blankness of earth, wood, tile, or stone; on meeting conditions, the mind remains settled, grasps nothing, and abides neither in contamination nor in its absence.

Senses.Explanation: In ordinary lexical use, the word marks an act or correspondence as lacking intent. A precept-case story has two monks report that one unintentionally committed sexual misconduct and the other unintentionally committed killing (一人無心氾淫，一人無心犯殺). A verse comment contrasts 'deliberately plant flowers' with 'unintentionally plant willows' (有意栽花，不如無心插柳). A preface says that earlier words and the writer's own words 'coincided unintentionally' (無心而自合), explicitly denying deliberate copying. These uses name absence of intent in an act; they are a different referent from the no-mind defined by Huangbo and Dahui.
Senses.Note: Three independent allowlisted sources attest ordinary lack of intent in rule-violation narrative, proverb, and authorship disclaimer. The graph string is identical to the primary Chan-loaded term, but a clean target for either sense cannot cover both referents without vagueness.

Occurrences.Kwic: 時二比丘共語曰：『我二人，一人無心氾淫，一人無心犯殺。』共往優波離尊者處懺悔
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A precept-case narrative has two monks distinguish unintentional sexual misconduct and unintentional killing before seeking a ruling.

Occurrences.Kwic: 拈云：有意栽花，不如無心插柳，誰知他人鼻孔，卻挂在自己眉毛上？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A comment quotes the contrast: deliberately planting flowers does not equal unintentionally planting willows.

Occurrences.Kwic: 今見昔人之語，與朕之所言，多不約而暗符，無心而自合。圓音如是，不禁啞然。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A preface says earlier sayings and the writer's own wording agreed without prior arrangement and coincided unintentionally.

AlternateTargets: no-thought as the axiom (無念為宗)
Senses.Explanation: No (無) plus thought (念): 'no-thought.' The axiom the Platform Sutra sets up first among three pillars: 'we set up no-thought as the axiom, no-form as the substance, no-abiding as the root' (先立無念為宗，無相為體，無住為本). The Sutra defines it by parallel — 'no-form: amid forms, free of forms; no-thought: amid thought, no-thought' (無相者，於相而離相。無念者，於念而無念) — thoughts keep flowing ('thought after thought continuing' 念念相續) while the mind is not stained by what it meets ('on all objects, the mind unstained' 於諸境上，心不染). And it rejects the reading that one thinks of nothing at all: 'if you think of nothing at all, forcing thought to stop, that is bondage, a one-sided view' (若百物不思，當令念絕，即是法縛，即名邊見). Huineng grounds it against people who quote 'see the nature' and then let thought breed wrong views: 'why set up no-thought as the axiom? — because deluded people who only mouth "see the nature" have thought on objects, and on that thought wrong views arise' (云何立無念為宗？只緣口說見性，迷人於境上有念，念上便起邪見). His disciple Shenhui taught it as 'the no-thought teaching' (無念法) and, pressed whether it 'exists,' refused both horns: 'the no-thought teaching says neither is nor is-not' (無念法不言有，不言無). By these definitions, then, no-thought is had in the middle of thought ('amid thought, no-thought' 於念而無念), the mind unstained (心不染) — not the extinction of thought, which the text itself calls bondage (法縛). The Zongbao recension also defines it character by character — 'no — no what thing? thought — thought of what thing? no: no dual marks, none of the dust-and-toil mind; thought: thought of the true-thus original nature; true-thusness is the body of thought, thought is the functioning of true-thusness' (無者無何事？念者念何物？無者無二相，無諸塵勞之心。念者念真如本性。真如即是念之體，念即是真如之用) — and by non-staining: 'on all objects the mind unstained: that is called no-thought; in one's own thought always free of the objects, not raising mind on the object' (於諸境上，心不染，曰無念。於自念上，常離諸境，不於境上生心) (both T48n2008). The Sutra equates it with complete command of wisdom ('this is complete command of wisdom; this is no-thought' 即是般若三昧，即是無念, T48n2008; Dunhuang: 'awakening to complete command of wisdom is no-thought' 悟般若三昧，即是無念, T48n2007), names its carrying-out 'the no-thought conduct' (無念行: 'complete command of wisdom, unimpeded liberation, is named the no-thought conduct' 般若三昧、自在解脫，名無念行, T48n2008), repeats the anti-blankness warning as 'if a single thought is cut off you die and receive birth elsewhere — a great error' (一念絕即死，別處受生，是為大錯, T48n2008), and closes on the triplet 'one who awakens to the no-thought teaching: the myriad things all penetrated; sees the realm of the buddhas; arrives at the stage of a buddha' (悟無念法者，萬法盡通；悟無念法者，見諸佛境界；悟無念法者，至佛地位, T48n2008; T48n2007 with the variant 'one who awakens to the sudden no-thought teaching' 悟無念頓法者).
Senses.Note: Center of gravity is the Platform Sutra, attested across two independent recensions (T48n2008, the Zongbao recension 宗寶本, and T48n2007, the Dunhuang recension 敦煌本), plus Shenhui's record (B25n0143) — Huineng's disciple and the teaching's great advocate. Yongming Yanshou's Records of the Source-Mirror (宗鏡錄, T48n2016) quotes it heavily too. Anti-fakeout: do NOT render no-thought (無念) as 'no thoughts / mental blankness' — the primary texts explicitly call that reading bondage (法縛). RelatedTerms no-form (無相) and no-abiding (無住) are its two companion pillars; 'no-thought as the axiom' (無念為宗) is the standing formula. Zen-allowlist grep counts: no-thought (無念), 810 hits in 143 of 462 texts; 'no-thought as the axiom' (無念為宗) 33, 'the no-thought teaching' (無念法) 23, 'awaken to the no-thought teaching' (悟無念法) 13, 'set up no-thought' (立無念) 8. The 'one who awakens to the no-thought teaching' (悟無念法者) triplet itself recurs quoted in the Records of the Source-Mirror (宗鏡錄, T48n2016), the Imperially Selected Recorded Sayings (御選語錄, X68n1319), and a Ming recorded-sayings collection (J34nB301) — the founding formulas travel through the later record verbatim.

Occurrences.Kwic: 無相者，於相而離相。無念者，於念而無念。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Platform Sutra of the Sixth Ancestor's Teaching Treasure (六祖大師法寶壇經, Zongbao recension); Huineng's own definition-by-parallel: 'no-form: amid forms, free of forms; no-thought: amid thought, no-thought.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 若百物不思，當令念絕，即是法縛，即名邊見。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The explicit anti-blankness clause — 'no-thought' is not the cessation of thought: thinking of nothing at all, forcing thought to stop, is called bondage (法縛) and a one-sided view (邊見).

Occurrences.Kwic: 善知識！云何立無念為宗？只緣口說見性，迷人於境上有念，念上便起邪見，一切塵勞妄想從此而生。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Why no-thought is 'set up as the axiom' (立無念為宗) — grounded in the text's own reason: deluded people who only mouth 'see the nature' (口說見性) have thought on objects, and wrong views arise on that thought.

Occurrences.Kwic: 何名無念？無念法者，見一切法，不著一切法；遍一切處，不著一切處。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Platform Sutra of the Southern School's Sudden Teaching (南宗頓教…壇經, Dunhuang recension) — independent witness: no-thought = seeing all things yet sticking to none, present everywhere yet stuck nowhere.

Occurrences.Kwic: 禪師日常說無念法，勸人修學，未審無念法有無？答曰：無念法不言有，不言無。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Shenhui (Huineng's disciple) answering the Duke of Yan, Zhang (張燕公), in the Shenhui documents — asked whether the no-thought teaching (無念法) exists or not, he answers: it 'says neither is nor is-not' (不言有，不言無).

Senses.Explanation: Literally "no birth" or "not arising" (無生): "unborn," attested 4,980 times in 383 allowlisted texts. The corpus uses it as predicate, noun, phrase label, song title, and part of longer compounds. In the Yongjia encounter, a patriarch asks, "why not embody the unborn and comprehend what has no speed?" Yongjia answers, "embodiment itself is unborn; comprehension originally has no speed" (何以體取無生，了無速乎；體即無生，了本無速). A later formal address asks, "what is a phrase of the unborn?" (如何是無生底句). Yang Jie writes, "why spend idle effort and further speak sayings of the unborn?" (討甚閒工夫，更說無生話), an explicit critical deployment. Another address turns the term against fixation: "when the mind dwells in the unborn, the unborn itself is birth and death," then raises the staff and says, "this is not the unborn" (心住，無生即生死；拈拄杖，云：這箇不是無生). In a raised case, being recognized earns banishment "into the country of the unborn," which is immediately rejected as dead water that holds no dragon. The record also joins the term to Chan action in "endurance of the unborn beneath the staff" (棒下無生忍). These constructions state or work directly on no birth or arising; the entry does not replace them with a broader framework.
Senses.Note: Counted forms: "originally unborn" (本無生), 326; "endurance concerning no arising" (無生法忍), 217; "unborn and unextinguished" (無生無滅), 92. The longer compounds are translated literally and not assumed to control every bare-headword occurrence. Personal names containing the graphs are excluded when context identifies a person.

Occurrences.Kwic: 何以體取無生，了無速乎？曰：體即無生，了本無速。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Yongjia case: "why not embody the unborn and comprehend what has no speed?—embodiment itself is unborn; comprehension originally has no speed." Two speakers, so unlinked.

Occurrences.Kwic: 且道：如何是無生底句？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Gu Xuezhe's address asks: "tell me, what is a phrase of the unborn?" No validated roster link is used.

Occurrences.Kwic: 討甚閒工夫，更說無生話。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Yang Jie writes: "why spend idle effort and further speak sayings of the unborn?" Biographical verse, so unlinked.

Occurrences.Kwic: 假借四大以為身。心本無生因境有。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Transmitted verse: "borrow the four great elements to make a body; the mind is originally unborn and exists because of objects." Quoted verse remains unlinked.

Occurrences.Kwic: 有能恁麼搆去，便謂立證無生，不待僧祗而成正覺。如今要見無生麼？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A public address says that understanding in this way is immediately realizing the unborn, then asks whether the assembly wants to see the unborn.

Occurrences.Kwic: 精金應不變為塵，一悟無生永不錯。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A verse says that once the unborn is awakened to, it is never mistaken.

Occurrences.Kwic: 無生無滅，是如來清淨禪；諸法空寂，是如來清淨坐。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: An address pairs unborn and unextinguished and predicates that this is the Tathagata's pure Chan.

Occurrences.Kwic: 且道如何是無生義？」良久，云：「分明渾若太虛空
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A master asks for the meaning of the unborn, pauses, and begins the recorded answer with a comparison to vast empty space.

Occurrences.Kwic: 真云：識破後如何？山云：貶向無生國裏。真云：莫是他安身立命處麼？山云：死水不藏龍。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: In a raised Liangshan case, recognition is followed by banishment into the country of the unborn; when asked whether this is a place to settle one's life, the master replies that dead water holds no dragon.

Occurrences.Kwic: 上堂。半夜子心住，無生即生死。拈拄杖，云：這箇不是無生。卓一下，云：生死向什麼處去也？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A formal address warns that dwelling in the unborn makes the unborn itself birth and death; the master raises the staff, says it is not the unborn, strikes once, and asks where birth and death have gone.

Occurrences.Kwic: 莫道百千萬億文殊，便是百千萬億世尊也下一槌擯出。不見道：棒下無生忍，臨機不見師。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: An address says that even countless Manjushris and World-Honored Ones would be struck and expelled, then cites 'endurance of the unborn beneath the staff; at the encounter, no master is seen.'

Senses.Explanation: Literally "without" (無) "marks, appearance, or form" (相): "without marks" or "markless," attested within 2,588 total occurrences across 324 allowlisted texts. Huineng's Platform Record gives a direct definition: "markless means being among marks while apart from marks" (無相者，於相而離相). It also says the teaching establishes "marklessness as its body" (無相為體, 11 occurrences). A later small assembly quotes that three-part formula and asks why marklessness is not also made the source. In a Compendium encounter, a monk asks, "what is without marks?" and the master answers, "mountains green, waters verdant" (如何是無相；山青水綠). Transmission wording places "true form, markless" (實相無相, 103) between "the subtle mind of extinction" and "subtle correct teaching." The corpus further records Mazu asking how to accord with "markless complete command" (無相三昧). These definitions, questions, compounds, and quotations keep the phrase tied to marks and their absence; this entry does not turn it into an imported theory.
Senses.Note: The source text's two-graph term can be adjectival or nominal. The direct "among marks while apart from marks" definition occurs in two Platform Record witnesses. The homographic title-name Wuxiang is separated below.

Occurrences.Kwic: 無相者，於相而離相。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Huineng's Platform Record directly defines: "markless means being among marks while apart from marks."

Occurrences.Kwic: 問。如何是無相。師曰。山青水綠。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: In layman Pangyun's section: "what is without marks?—mountains green, waters verdant." The answer speaker is not safely linked from this excerpt.

Occurrences.Kwic: 吾以清淨法眼涅槃妙心實相無相微妙正法將付於汝
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Transmission quotation: "I will entrust to you the pure eye of the teaching, subtle mind of extinction, true form that is markless, and subtle correct teaching." Historical quotation remains unlinked.

Occurrences.Kwic: 早叅舉六祖大師無相為體無念為本無住為宗師云既云無相為體何不即以無相為宗既云無念為本何不即以無念為宗
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A later small assembly quotes the Sixth Patriarch's 'marklessness as body' formula and asks why marklessness is not also made the source.

Occurrences.Kwic: 遂問。如何用心即合無相三昧。讓曰。汝學心地法門如下種子。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Dahui's instruction recounts Mazu asking how to accord with 'markless complete command'; Nanyue begins his recorded answer with the field of mind and a seed.

Senses.Explanation: As a personal name, Wuxiang is the Yizhou master named in lineage headings. The Linked Lamps lists "one lineage heir of Master Wuxiang of Yizhou" (益州無相禪師法嗣一人), namely Wuzhu of Baotang in the following text. Two independent lamp histories likewise place Baotang Wuzhu under this heading and say that Wuzhu first received the teaching from Master Wuxiang (初得法於無相大師). These occurrences name a person and must not be translated as the adjective "markless."
Senses.Note: The full string "Wuxiang of Yizhou" (益州無相) occurs 17 times and "Master Wuxiang" (無相禪師) 18. Three curated witnesses establish the same Yizhou-master/Baotang-Wuzhu lineage relation; unrelated people who may also bear the name are not silently identified with him.

Occurrences.Kwic: 益州無相禪師法嗣一人
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Lineage heading: "one lineage heir of Master Wuxiang of Yizhou." The master has no exact roster primary name used here.

Occurrences.Kwic: 益州保唐寺無住禪師初得法於無相大師。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Under the Yizhou Wuxiang lineage heading, the record says that Master Wuzhu of Baotang first received the teaching from Master Wuxiang.

Occurrences.Kwic: 益州保唐寺無住禪師。初得法於無相大師。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: An independent lamp history likewise names Wuzhu of Baotang and says that he first received the teaching from Master Wuxiang.

Senses.Explanation: Literally, 'precepts without form.' The phrase occurs 10 times in 5 allowlisted texts. The Platform Record places it at the center of Huineng's public teaching: he mounts the high seat and confers the formless precepts on a gathering of monastics, officials, scholars, and laypeople, then tells the assembly that each must receive them in their own person and repeat after him. A preface to another recension defines them with the exact formula 'formless precepts: precepts concerning necessary correct awakening' and calls them 'the foremost of precepts.' A later public interview asks, 'What are the formless precepts?' and records the teacher striking the questioner. In this Zen deployment the phrase is not a relaxation of rules; it names a publicly conferred precept form directed to each recipient's own person and also becomes the subject of direct testing in the hall.
Senses.Note: The two Platform recensions are related witnesses, but the phrase also occurs in three other allowlisted files. Claims here are restricted to the direct wording and ceremony preserved by the Platform texts.

Occurrences.Kwic: 兼授無相戒弘法弟子法海集記第一折惠能大師於大梵寺講堂中，昇高座，說摩訶般若波羅蜜法，授無相戒。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Platform Record introduces Huineng mounting the high seat and conferring the formless precepts.

Occurrences.Kwic: 善知識！總須自體與受無相戒。一時，逐惠能口道，令善知識見自三身佛
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Huineng tells the whole assembly to receive the formless precepts in their own person and repeat after him.

Occurrences.Kwic: 無相戒者，戒其必正覺也。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A Platform recension's preface supplies a direct definition formula.

Occurrences.Kwic: 無相戒，戒之最也；四弘願，願之極也；無相懺，懺之至也。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The same preface explicitly appraises the formless precepts as the foremost of precepts.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師請圓戒，童諾。師隨問云：「如何是無相戒？」童便打，師云：「久知有這一棒。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A later interview turns the formless precepts into a direct question and records a blow as the response.

Senses.Explanation: Literally, "without words." In its dominant narrative deployment it is an encounter stage direction rendered "had no reply": after a question, answer, gesture, or demand to speak, a named person or assembled community gives no answer. The term occurs 4,794 times in 370 allowlisted texts, and "the monk had no reply" (僧無語) alone occurs 2,043 times. The record may then continue with another question, a blow, dismissal, or an appraisal. One assembly has no reply after being told to speak and the master breaks the jar; Linji asks a scripture lecturer "where is the buddha?" and dismisses him after he has no reply; another master appraises a monk's wordlessness as "a real patch-robed monk" (真箇衲僧). The same graph sequence occurs inside the longer phrase "no verbal phrases" (無語句) in Deshan's transmitted statement, "our school has no verbal phrases and truly not a single teaching to give anyone" (我宗無語句，實無一法與人). Dahui later quotes and criticizes that statement. Both deployments state absence of words; the following graph "phrases" (句) supplies the object in the longer compound and does not create a second lexical referent for "without words" (無語).
Senses.Note: The public-interview stage direction is the dominant use. The longer 'no verbal phrases' formula and its later criticism remain included as a distinct deployment shape within the same lexical sense. Neither form automatically means that a person was enlightened, defeated, mentally blank, or committed to silence as a defining position.

Occurrences.Kwic: 祖曰。甚麼物恁麼來。師無語。遂經八載。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Sixth Patriarch asks, "what thing comes thus?" The interlocutor has no reply; the narrative then says eight years passed.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師以拄杖指醬瓮云道得即不打破道不得即打破眾無語師便打破歸方丈。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The master points to the sauce jar and says it will be spared if they can speak; the assembly has no reply, and he breaks it and returns to his quarters.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師云：「佛在什麼處？」主無語。師云：「對常侍前擬瞞老僧，速退速退，妨他別人諸問。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Linji asks a scripture lecturer, "where is the buddha?" The lecturer has no reply and Linji dismisses him so others can question.

Occurrences.Kwic: 頭云：蒼天！蒼天！峯無語，回舉似師，師云：汝更去見伊道：蒼天！蒼天！汝便噓兩聲。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Shitou says, "heavens, heavens!" Deng Yinfeng has no reply and returns to report the exchange to his teacher.

Occurrences.Kwic: 曰：莫是學人著力處也無？師曰：歸宗拽石。僧無語。師曰：真箇衲僧。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: After a monk asks whether this is where a student exerts effort, the master answers 'Guizong drags a stone'; the monk has no reply, and the master says, 'a real patch-robed monk.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 至明日請益。師曰。我宗無語句。實無一法與人。峯因此有省。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The lamp record transmits Deshan's statement, "our school has no verbal phrases; truly not a single teaching to give anyone."

Occurrences.Kwic: 古人道。我宗無語句。實無一法與人。恁麼道。早是通身浸在屎窖裏了也。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Dahui quotes the old saying and immediately criticizes saying it: "already immersed bodily in a cesspit."

Occurrences.Kwic: 示眾，舉德山和尚因僧問：從上諸聖以何法示人？山云：我宗無語句，亦無一法與人。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A later formal address explicitly introduces and quotes Deshan's response to the question, "by what teaching did the sages of old show people?"
